info.bio:
Bronski Beat se formó en 1983, año en que Somerville, Steinbachek y Bronski compartieron una casa de Lancaster, en Brixton, al sudoeste de Londres. El nombre de la banda era al parecer “dios prohibido” antes de que Bronski Beat fuera sugerido por Steve.

El grupo firmó un contrato de grabación en Londres en 1984 después de que solamente hizo 9 hits en vivo. El primer single llegó al número 3 en el Reino Unido. Smalltown Boy, la historia sobre de un muchacho que fue echado lejos por su familia y vecinos por ser gay.

scenes.name: Frankie Goes to Hollywood
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: Veteranos de la escena glam punk del Eric's (Holly Johnson de Big in Japan, Paul Rutherford de los Spitfire Boys) más «the lads», con imagen sadomasoquista y homosexualidad declarada: los «Disco Pistols». Atrapados en un contrato humillante con ZTT, Horn graba «Relax» (1983) casi sin ellos, a ritmo de Hi-NRG con Fairlight y Linn sincronizados; la prohibición de la BBC la lleva al número uno. Morley planea una trilogía sobre sexo, guerra y religión: «Two Tribes» (nueve semanas en el número uno, con camisetas «FRANKIE SAY»), «The Power of Love». Welcome to the Pleasuredome decepciona, Estados Unidos los ve como unos Village People y acaban sin fans de verdad: anuncio del regreso de las boy bands. «¿No tuvieron alguna vez la sensación de que los engañaron?»

mentions.author: Simon Reynolds
mentions.text: …del popper. Frankie Goes to Hollywood fue el primer grupo que se animó a hacerlo, junto con sus vecinos de Liverpool Pete Burns, de Dead or Alive, y Bronski Beat. Estos últimos, quienes supuestamente rechazaron las ofertas de ZTT, representaban el lado más responsable del orgullo gay, la lucha por la dignidad frente a la intolerancia. Johnson y Rutherford, en cambio, eran hedonistas de pura cepa, y mucho más intimidantes. El cantante de Bronski Beat, Jimmy Somerville, si bien tenía un look distinguido, se vestía con jeans y camisas comunes y corrientes, lo que dejaba entender que los integrantes…

podcast.title: Groundbreaking Gay Positive Band
podcast.body: Bronski Beat was recognized as a groundbreaking "gay positive band" in the early 1980s, featuring Richard Coles on keyboards and Jimmy Somerville as the singer. "That eventually led to a job playing keyboards for the groundbreaking gay positive band Bronsky beat in the early 80s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Jimmy Somerville's Personal Connection to "Small Town Boy"
podcast.body: The video for "Small Town Boy" featured singer Jimmy Somerville, who personally experienced the same kinds of bullying, estrangement from family, and rejection depicted in the song and its visual narrative. This personal connection added authenticity and emotional weight to the song's message. "You couldn't help but feel terrible for the character played by singer Jimmy Somerville, who by the way experienced the same sort of things that we see in the video, the bullying, the estrangement from family, and the rejection."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Early Days of LGBTQ Rock

podcast.title: Motivation for Honest Gay Songs
podcast.body: The band started by playing local arts festivals and became increasingly frustrated with how "sanitized and safe" other gay performers were. This frustration fueled their mission to write honest songs directly addressing the realities of being gay, including the politics, social challenges, and abuse faced by the LGBTQ community. "Everything was to write honest songs about being gay, the politics involved, the social challenges, and the abuse the LGBTQ community faced."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Early Days of LGBTQ Rock

podcast.title: Openly Gay Trio from Glasgow
podcast.body: Bronski Beat was a synth rock trio from Glasgow in the early to mid-1980s, a period and place described as bleak and challenging for openly gay individuals. All three members of the band were openly gay, making their public presence particularly brave. "They were a synth rock trio from Glasgow, a pretty bleak place in the early 80s and mid-80s, and a tough place to be openly gay, as all three members of the band were."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Early Days of LGBTQ Rock

podcast.title: Post-Peak Technopop Persistence
podcast.body: As the popularity of pure Technopop waned in the mid-1980s, Bronski Beat was noted as a group that, along with their spin-off The Communards, continued to stand their ground and maintain a presence with their electronic sound. "Bronski beat and their spin off the Comming Arts stood their ground."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Quick Record Deal with London Records
podcast.body: Bronski Beat secured a record deal with London Records after performing only nine gigs, indicating their immediate impact and appeal to the industry. "It took them all of nine gigs to get a record deal with London Records."

podcast.title: Technopop Descendant
podcast.body: Listed as one of the artists who descended from the original Technopop scene. "There was Bronsky beat, aha, yellow, Elfaville, Frankie Ghost of Hollywood. They all descended from the original Tecno Pop scene."

xref.title: Early Life and Music Career
xref.body: Richard Coles began his musical journey as a choir boy and later moved into theater. He became the keyboardist for the "groundbreaking gay positive band" Bronski Beat in the early 80s, and then followed singer Jimmy Somerville to form The Communards, where he also played keyboards. "Growing up, he was a choir boy before moving on to theater."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Personal Experiences Reflected in "Small Town Boy"
xref.body: As the singer for Bronski Beat, Jimmy Somerville's personal experiences, including bullying, estrangement from family, and rejection, directly informed and were portrayed in the powerful song and video for "Small Town Boy." "Jimmy Somerville, who by the way experienced the same sort of things that we see in the video, the bullying, the estrangement from family, and the rejection."

"Bronski beat and their spin off the Comming Arts stood their ground."
